classification.difficultyReason: Use the equal-segment marks to construct a symbolic length proof, then recognise that all three tangent ratios share ED as their denominator. The supplied length identity and 'hence' cue guide the connection, but the student must translate it into a trigonometric proof.

spec.description: A, B, C and D occur in that order on a horizontal baseline, with E vertically above D. AE, BE, CE and DE are drawn. Matching double ticks on AB and BC show equality, and a right-angle marker at D shows AD perpendicular to DE. Decorative blue strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: AB = BC; A, B, C and D are collinear; AD is perpendicular to DE. Coordinates determine only the drawing and supply no numerical measurements.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence, deduce that $\tan\angle DEB=\frac{1}{2}\tan\angle AED+\frac{1}{2}\tan\angle CED$.

answer.short:
$\tan\angle DEB=\frac{BD}{ED}=\frac12\left(\frac{AD}{ED}+\frac{CD}{ED}\right)=\frac12\tan\angle AED+\frac12\tan\angle CED$.

Use $\tan\theta=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$ in the three right-angled triangles and substitute the result of part a.
answer.worked:
Each triangle is right-angled at $D$. Using opposite divided by adjacent relative to its angle at $E$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\angle DEB&=\frac{BD}{ED}\\\tan\angle AED&=\frac{AD}{ED}\\\tan\angle CED&=\frac{CD}{ED}.\end{align*}$$
Using part a:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\angle DEB&=\frac{\frac12(AD+CD)}{ED}\\\tan\angle DEB&=\frac12\frac{AD}{ED}+\frac12\frac{CD}{ED}\\\tan\angle DEB&=\frac12\tan\angle AED+\frac12\tan\angle CED.\end{align*}$$
